profile_text.body:
AI Now Institute, founded in 2017, is a nonprofit policy research organization headquartered in New York, NY. According to its website, the institute challenges and reimagines the current trajectory for AI, producing research that maps the state of the AI market, interrogates the industry's key sources of power, and provides actionable strategies to reclaim public agency over the future of AI.

The institute's work focuses on AI governance and risk. Chief AI Scientist Heidy Khlaaf, who left OpenAI in 2021, has published research arguing that trusting companies to self-report the risks of their own products constitutes both a conflict of interest and a "subversion of democratic processes when AI labs are allowed to take over the arbitration of risk determinations with life-or-death consequences." The institute also examines how algorithmic wages and prices are reshaping economic systems, and has critiqued the AI industry's failure to apply established safety and security protocols from other sectors.
